title: ISO 27001 framework version badge not rendered — `ControlMappingTable.jsx` badge only renders for `aws_/azure_/gcp_/k8s_` prefixes; ISO 27001 version silently hidden; auditors cannot distinguish 2013 (114 controls) from 2022 (93 controls)
12+ console.log statements leak project IDs to browser console in production — `EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx`, `AutoCollectorsContent.jsx`; violates A.8.16 information disclosure in logs
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx`, `AutoCollectorsContent.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Development-era `console.log` calls were never removed from both components. They log internal project identifiers, organization IDs, and API response payloads to the browser DevTools console in production builds, violating A.8.16 (information in application logs).
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. In EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx, remove all console.log calls (approximately 6–8 statements).
2. In AutoCollectorsContent.jsx, remove all console.log calls (approximately 4–6 statements).
3. Run: grep -rn "console.log" src/components/evidence-management/ and fix any remaining instances.
4. Add ESLint rule to prevent future occurrences: "no-console": "error" in the project's .eslintrc.js.
```

title: No due date or SLA field on evidence requests — `CreateEvidenceRequestDrawer` collects no `dueDate`; overdue requests indistinguishable from recently created ones; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/CreateEvidenceRequestDrawer.jsx`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-request.model.js`
**Root Cause:** The request creation form collects title, description, and assignee but no `dueDate` field. The schema likely has no required `dueDate`. Without a due date, no overdue indicator, SLA tracking, or automated reminder is possible.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
Backend — evidence-request.model.js:
1. Add: dueDate: { type: Date, required: true }
2. Add server-side validation: dueDate: Joi.date().min('now').required()

Frontend — CreateEvidenceRequestDrawer.jsx:
3. Add <DatePicker label="Due Date" required /> field.
4. Client-side validation: if (!dueDate || dueDate < new Date()) setError('Due date must be in the future').

Frontend — EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx:
5. Add overdue badge:
   const isOverdue = req.dueDate && new Date() > new Date(req.dueDate) && req.status !== 'fulfilled';
   if (isOverdue) render <Badge color="red">Overdue — {daysOverdue}d</Badge>
```

title: Analytics export button not implemented — Download button in `AnalyticsContent.jsx` has no implementation; auditors cannot export analytics as management review artefacts; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/AnalyticsContent.jsx` — Download button
**Root Cause:** The Download button in `AnalyticsContent.jsx` was added as a UI placeholder during development. No `onClick` handler was implemented; clicking it does nothing.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/AnalyticsContent.jsx

In the Download button onClick:
1. Collect analytics data from component state (coverage %, status counts, review times, framework breakdown).
2. Build a CSV:
   const csvRows = [headers, ...dataRows].map(r => r.join(',')).join('\n');
3. Trigger download:
   const blob = new Blob([csvRows], { type: 'text/csv' });
   const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
   const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = url; a.download = `evidence-analytics-${date}.csv`; a.click();
4. Include in CSV: Framework, Coverage%, Mapped, Total, Evidence by Status, Avg Review Time (days), Export Date.
```

title: No ISO 27001 Annex A control reference per integration evidence item — `IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx` shows no MODEL_TO_ANNEX_A mapping; auditors cannot determine which Annex A control each integration evidence satisfies
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Integration evidence items (from Okta, GitHub, Jira, AWS Security Hub, etc.) are displayed without their associated ISO 27001 Annex A control references. The backend integration workers map evidence to control IDs internally, but `IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx` never renders an "Annex A Control" column.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx

1. Add MODEL_TO_ANNEX_A mapping object:
   const MODEL_TO_ANNEX_A = {
     'okta_user': ['A.5.15', 'A.5.16'], 'github_commit': ['A.8.32'],
     'aws_finding': ['A.8.8', 'A.8.20'], 'jira_ticket': ['A.8.19'], ...
   };
2. Add "Annex A Controls" column to the table.
3. Render each control reference as a badge: <Badge>{control}</Badge>.
4. If no mapping exists, render a "Map to Control" button linking to ControlMappingContent.
5. Ensure backend integration evidence endpoint returns `annex_a_controls: string[]` per item.
```

title: Export formats silently fail with generic error toast — `handleExport` catches errors with no indication which formats are implemented; auditors preparing ZIP bundles before certification get silent failures; violates Clause 7.5.3

Mandatory reviewer note missing in AI metadata validation drawer — `resolutionNotes` Textarea in `EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx` is optional with no minimum length; accepted metadata with no trail; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx` — `resolutionNotes` Textarea
**Root Cause:** The `resolutionNotes` field in the AI metadata validation drawer is optional — reviewers can approve or reject AI-parsed metadata with an empty note. This mirrors EM-002 but applies to AI-assisted upload validation, where justification is equally critical for traceability.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx

1. In the submit handler, add before API call:
   if (!resolutionNotes || resolutionNotes.trim().length < 30) {
     setNoteError('Resolution note required (min 30 characters)'); return;
   }
2. Pass error and helperText to Textarea.
3. Backend AI validation endpoint: add resolutionNotes: Joi.string().min(30).required()
```

title: Google Drive Bearer token sent directly to connector service origin — JWT from `state.auth.token` in raw `fetch()` to `CS_URL` in `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx`; bypasses Next.js API proxy; CORS failure likely in production; violates A.8.20
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/GDriveFileBrowser.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx` calls `fetch(CS_URL, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token } })` using the raw JWT from Redux state. `CS_URL` is the connector service origin (a different domain). This bypasses the Next.js API proxy, violates CORS policy in production, and exposes the user's JWT to a cross-origin endpoint.
**Impact:** CORS preflight will fail in production, breaking Google Drive integration entirely. The JWT could be intercepted or misused by the connector service.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. Create Next.js API route: pages/api/evidence/gdrive-files.js
   — Accepts GET with query params
   — Adds Authorization header server-side (use service account or exchange JWT)
   — Proxies to connector service, returns response

2. In GDriveFileBrowser.jsx, replace:
   fetch(CS_URL, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token } })
   with:
   fetch('/api/evidence/gdrive-files?' + queryParams)

3. Remove direct CS_URL reference from the component.
4. Add CSRF token validation in the API route.
```
